label: first n/j/u/h/1/2/k/p during the original phase, after t or y
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase: 97.5% of activation mass. A small amount falls on the <DEL> step and none on copy steps. Never fires at t=0 or 1, and it peaks at t=3-5. It is driven by the current input token, mostly the first occurrence of n (8x lift, 31% of mass), then j, u, h, 1, 2, k and p. It is gated by context: rates are much higher when t or y (and to a lesser extent v, s, k, w) appeared earlier, especially as the first tokens. The top activations are all sequences starting with y t / t y and then n, j, u or h. The listed tokens rarely fire without that context, and repeated occurrences rarely fire. The predicate has low precision (many contexts with these tokens stay below threshold) and misses about 35% of mass from other tokens (z, f, r) or other contexts. This suggests a graded combination of input identity and prefix composition rather than a crisp rule. Magnitude is highest for n after an early t/y.
